New Zealand's Devon Conway, right, is caught behind by India wicketkeeper Rishabh Pant, left, during the fifth day of the first Test match in Wellington, New Zealand, on November 23, 2026. | Photo Credit: AP
The wind made its presence felt for the first time in the Test, and India made decent use of the conditions to pick up two wickets with the soft ball and keep its hopes of a rare victory in New Zealand alive.
Also read | IND vs NZ 1st Test Day 4: Jurel sees chance for India despite slowing Basin Reserve pitch
Washington Sundar and Prasidh Krishna struck to remove the two overnight unbeaten batters as New Zealand went into lunch at 157 for four, still 195 runs short of wiping out India’s first-innings deficit, on the final day of the first Test at Basin Reserve on Monday (November 23, 2026).
With the new ball still 35 overs away and eight wickets to get, Jasprit Bumrah was used in short bursts. It was Washington, however, who found the breakthrough in the 12 th over of the day, making the most of the wind blowing into him.
The off-spinner got one to drift into Devon Conway, the inside edge lobbed off the pad, allowing Rishabh Pant to stretch forward to his left and pouch a neat catch. Conway, who had battled through the final session on Sunday (November 22), scored 65 (165b, 7x4).
Four overs later, Prasidh got the better of Rachin Ravindra (37, 129b, 4x4). The left-hander, who had looked comfortable through the morning, pushed at a delivery in the channel outside off, offering K.L. Rahul the opportunity to stretch to his left in the air at widish second slip, the only fielder in the cordon, and take the catch.
Daryl Mitchell and Tom Blundell, however, were in no mood to let the session slip away. The pair negotiated the remaining overs without much fuss, keeping India’s attack at bay and ensuring there was no further damage before lunch.
With the new ball nine overs away, India will hope the harder cherry brings the extra pace, bounce and movement needed to prise the remaining wickets.
India 720/9 declared. New Zealand 368 and 157/4; 71 overs (Devon Conway 65, Rachin Ravindra 37).
